Salmon Bank Selects Profinch to Automate BSP Regulatory Reporting
summary:
Salmon Bank (Rural Bank) Inc. has selected Profinch Solutions Pte. Ltd. to automate its regulatory reporting to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), deploying Profinch's BSP Regulatory Reporting platform.
The engagement centers on two deliverables:
The first is the Financial Reporting Package (FRP) and its supporting schedules, covering the bank's current submissions under FRP V15, alongside readiness for FRP V16, which the BSP has deferred to 30th June 2027 to give banks additional time to prepare their people, processes, and systems.
The second is the Comprehensive Credit and Equity Exposures Report (COCREE 2.0), the BSP's granular borrower- and counterparty-level exposure return, which carries substantially higher data volumes and validation requirements than aggregated reports.
The platform automates business, schema, and rule-based validation. It also generates BSP-ready XML output for submission, with maker-checker workflows and exception dashboards enforcing review at every stage. It is deployed within Salmon Bank's own Cloud infrastructure in a dedicated, isolated configuration built exclusively for the Bank, leaving Salmon Bank in full control of its infrastructure and production data at all times.
Raffy Montemayor, Deputy CEO at Salmon Bank (Rural Bank) commented, "At Salmon Bank, we continue to invest in technology that strengthens operational efficiency and regulatory compliance. Working with Profinch enables us to modernize our regulatory reporting process with a structured and scalable approach that supports our compliance objectives while providing a foundation for future regulatory initiatives."
Nikhil Deshmukh, Business Head - Enterprise Apps, Asia-Pacific, Profinch commented, "Financial institutions today are looking to strengthen regulatory reporting with greater consistency, transparency, and operational efficiency while keeping pace with evolving regulatory expectations. We are pleased to partner with Salmon Bank and to support the bank with a secure, cloud-native solution that simplifies validation, strengthens governance, and enables accurate BSP-compliant XML generation."
This engagement represents another milestone in Profinch's growing presence across Southeast Asia, reinforcing its commitment to helping financial institutions modernize regulatory reporting through cloud-native, enterprise-grade banking technology solutions.
Chaitanya Kashyap, Global Business Head – Enterprise Apps at Profinch commented, "The conversation around regulatory reporting has fundamentally shifted. It is no longer a tactical exercise of meeting the next deadline, but a strategic imperative to build systems capable of adapting to tomorrow's template changes and regulatory asks. Across Southeast Asia and our global markets, we see a growing demand for this level of architectural resilience. We are proud to provide Salmon Bank with an enterprise-grade foundation that helps future-proof their compliance operations."

PNC Bank Expands Branch Buildout to More Than 370, With Plans to Build 60 Branches Per Year
summary:
PNC Bank today announced it will broaden its branch expansion to more than 370 total new locations by 2031, including more than 70 branches already opened since announcing its original expansion strategy. The additional branches will strengthen PNC's presence across the Southeast, adding more than 50 new locations in South Carolina and Georgia, underscoring the company's commitment to two of the nation's fastest-growing states. In addition, given the success PNC has experienced in its previously announced expansion markets, the company plans to build an additional 10 locations across Texas, Florida and North Carolina.
 
Flower Mound Interior






As part of this approximately $2.5 billion investment in its network, PNC plans to open 60 branches per year from 2027 onward while renovating its existing locations across all markets, reinforcing its commitment to delivering exceptional in-branch hospitality across the country. In total, PNC expects to hire 2,400 employees as part of this expansion, bringing more bankers into more communities to support the in-person needs of more clients.
"We're seeing strong demand for the incredible hospitality, advice and personalized service that our bankers provide across the country every day," said Jeff Martinez, head of Branch Distribution and Sales Management at PNC. "The positive feedback and strong results have reinforced our confidence in doubling down on our expansion strategy and continuing to grow our network. These new branches will help us continue to deepen relationships, expand access to our advice, expertise and capabilities and make it easier for clients to bank with us however they choose."

title: Pennies Celebrates £90 Million Raised Through Micro-Donations and Announces 2026 Award Winners
summary:
Pennies, the UK’s leading micro-donation charity, hosted its annual Autumn Celebration Event in London, recognising the individuals and partners driving progress across the micro-donation movement. 
Held in central London and attended by over 150 leaders from retail, hospitality, payments and technology, the event celebrated Pennies’ growing community of partners – and highlighted its collective social impact to date: over 360 million micro-donations raised, delivering more than £90 million for over 1,150 UK charities. 
The event was made possible with the support of Stripe, event sponsor, alongside award sponsors Intuit, NashTech, Taggstar, Experian and Worldpay, all of whom play an important role in supporting and championing the growing micro-donation movement.
2026 Pennies Award Winners 
The 7th annual Pennies Awards honoured both organisations and individuals who have gone above and beyond to integrate, scale and champion micro-donations across their customer experience. 
The Merchant Impact Award was presented to Currys for making Pennies a core part of a major technology investment. It rolled out round-up prompts on around 4,000 Stripe terminals across 296 stores in just three months, took Pennies online, and has helped customers raise £1 million for the Digital Poverty Alliance. 
The Technology Impact Award went to Astound Digital for helping London Gatwick become the first UK airport to build micro-donations into its online car-parking checkout, raising around £100,000 across 71,000 donations for Air Ambulance Kent Surrey Sussex. 
The Merchant Breakthrough Award was won by Musgrave Northern Ireland for growing a six-store trial into a 72-store rollout by winning over independent retailers one conversation at a time. More than one million micro-donations have raised over £200,000 for Action Cancer, already beating its annual target. 
The Power of Partnership Award, a new award for 2026, was won by Retail Technology Show, celebrating ten years of Pennies as the show’s Gold Charity Partner. In that time, it has championed micro-donations to around 14,000 senior retail leaders each year and supported Pennies’ growth from around 60 partners to more than 200. 
The Unsung Hero Awards recognised Zoë Pritchard (Lidl GB), Richard Riley (Greene King), Katie Martin-Fagg and Jess Jones (Currys) and Team Majestic Giffnock led by manager Kathy Hughes – all key people behind the scenes making micro-donations happen. 
The Outstanding Achievement Award was awarded to Toolstation and the British Heart Foundation, recognising a record-breaking first 8 months of their 5-year partnership that made Pennies everybody’s business. More than 522,000 micro-donations raised over £200,000 from January to August 2026, matching Toolstation’s entire 2025 Pennies total, and more than 3,300 colleagues have now learned CPR. 
The Judges’ Award was presented to Worldpay in recognition of a 15-year partnership that has built Pennies into the card payments of many of the UK’s best-known brands. The judges felt Worldpay deserved special recognition with this award, as this year the partnership passed 100 million micro-donations, raising more than £25.8 million for charities in the UK and Ireland. 
 
The event included a live panel discussion hosted by reporter and presenter, Sally Bundock, featuring senior leaders from three major UK brands: 
Kari Daniels – CEO, SSP UK Ireland and Netherlands   
Verity Warnecke – Head of Sustainability & Charity, Matalan   
Steve Worboys – Chief Operating Officer, Holland & Barrett   
Together, the panel explored consumer confidence in a challenging economy, how great customer experience sets brands apart, and how embedding purpose at the checkout can turn everyday moments into real community impact.

Revolut Completes Fundraising Process, Establishing a $115 Billion Valuation
summary:
Revolut, the global financial leader with over 80 million retail customers, has today announced the close of its latest fundraising process, establishing a new company valuation of $115 billion USD.
The transaction was led by Glade Brook Capital Partners, Coatue, Durable Capital Partners, T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc.*, and Baillie Gifford. Underpinned by strong business fundamentals and rapid expansion into new international markets, the process attracted participation from both long-standing partners and new global investors.
The transaction coincides with rapid business momentum. Since the start of 2026, the company has launched banks in the UK, Mexico, Australia, and New Zealand, while securing banking licences in France, Colombia, and Argentina, alongside conditional US charter approval from the OCC. This builds on Revolut’s established European banking operations across 30 EEA markets. The expansion is underpinned by strong financial performance: 2025 revenue grew 46% to $6.0 billion (£4.5bn) and pre-tax profit climbed 57% to $2.3 billion (£1.7bn), expanding pre-tax margins to 38%.
This milestone underscores Revolut's global momentum as the company scales toward its long-term goal of serving over 100 million active customers across more than 100 countries.
Nik Storonsky, CEO & Founder of Revolut, commented: “Every bank we launch means more people get a better way to manage their money, wherever they live. Our team makes that happen, and employee ownership has been central to our culture from day one. That’s why we’ve once again given them the chance to share in the value they’ve created, as we work towards our next milestone of serving 100 million customers.”
Victor Stinga, CFO of Revolut, said: "The milestones achieved this year have been several years in the making. They allow us to strengthen our digital banking proposition in our core markets and pave the way for it reaching millions more customers beyond Europe. The confidence of our investors, both existing and new, reflects Revolut’s unique opportunity to build the first truly global bank."

TD Brings Its Global Asset Management Businesses Under One Name
summary:
TD Global Investment Solutions will now operate under the TD Asset Management (TDAM) name, creating one consistent global brand across the firm's institutional and retail asset management businesses. Additionally, Epoch Investment Partners, Inc. (TD Epoch) has changed its name to TD Asset Management (US) Inc. (TDAM US). Both TD Asset Management Inc. and TDAM US will offer their products and services under the TDAM name. The change applies across all markets and jurisdictions, bringing TDAM's asset management capabilities together under one global brand.
"Our unified brand creates a clearer market presence and a more consistent experience for our clients around the world," says David Sykes, Chief Executive Officer, TDAM and Executive Vice President, TD Bank Group. "By bringing our capabilities under one name, we can make it easier for clients to understand and access the breadth of investment expertise we offer."
Key Takeaways:
TD Global Investment Solutions will operate under the TDAM name.
TD Epoch has changed its name to TDAM US.
Under one brand, TDAM will continue to leverage its global capabilities to deliver disciplined investment management.
Our unified brand creates a clearer market presence and more consistent experience for clients globally.
A simpler, more connected experience for clients
These changes do not affect TDAM's investment approach. Investment teams, portfolio managers, investment philosophies, and service teams remain unchanged.
"Our focus at TDAM has always been to put our clients at the centre of everything we do. That commitment is reflected in how we innovate, pursue investment excellence and build strong relationships to tailor solutions that aim to deliver better outcomes and help clients achieve their investment goals," says Sykes.
Building on a legacy of trusted investment expertise
With over 35 years of investment experience, TDAM offers fundamental equity strategies, including free cash flow strategies, quantitative and passive equities, fixed income across credit qualities, global multi-asset and derivatives solutions, commodities, and, in certain jurisdictions, private markets, including real estate, infrastructure, private debt and mortgages.
Under the unified brand, TDAM will continue to deliver disciplined investment management and draw on its global capabilities to support a broad range of investment objectives.

Allianz Commercial Launches ‘Allianz Commercial 1893’ Direct Underwriting Syndicate at Lloyd’s
summary:
Allianz Commercial today announced plans to establish Allianz Commercial 1893, a new direct underwriting syndicate at Lloyd’s. Trading is expected to begin from January 1, 2027, subject to final regulatory approval, with in-principle approval from Lloyd’s already in place.
The new syndicate will give Allianz Commercial greater access to Specialty, facilities and selected MGA business at Lloyd’s.
This strengthens Allianz’s presence at Lloyd’s, the only insurance marketplace of its kind, with a long-established global reputation as a center for complex Specialty insurance. With a Gross Written Premium of £57.9 billion, Lloyd’s accounts for roughly half of the total London market.
Thomas Lillelund, CEO of Allianz Commercial, comments: “The new syndicate will establish a long-term direct underwriting presence for Allianz Commercial in one of the world’s leading Specialty markets. It will expand our access to specialist business and strengthen our ability to serve clients and brokers facing increasingly complex and international risks.”
Dawn Miller, Lloyd’s Chief Commercial Officer and CEO of Lloyd’s Americas, adds: “We are delighted to welcome this new Allianz syndicate to the Lloyd’s market. The decision to launch at Lloyd’s not only reflects our history of bringing together the world’s leading risk takers but is also a vote of confidence in the market’s unique advantages in servicing multinational, specialty, and complex risks at scale.”

title: Global Payments Named Commerce Technology Provider for University of Memphis Tigers
summary:
Global Payments Inc., a leading payment technology and software company that powers commerce for businesses of all sizes worldwide, today announced it has been selected as the Commerce Technology Provider for the University of Memphis Tigers. Genius, the flagship point-of-sale (POS) and business management platform from Global Payments®, will enable food and beverage operations at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, home of Memphis Tigers Football.
At Memphis Tigers football games and other stadium events, Genius helps keep concession lines moving when demand peaks, enabling fans to order, pay and get back to the action faster. Behind the scenes, its fast, reliable and secure capabilities are designed to give Memphis Athletics the stability and flexibility to manage large crowds, high order volumes and the operational demands of event day.
“The University of Memphis’ selection of Genius underscores the platform’s ability to perform in demanding stadium and venue environments,” said David Rumph, president of SMB for Global Payments. “When thousands of fans want to make purchases within a short window, every second matters. Genius helps operators serve more guests quickly and reliably, while helping fans spend less time waiting and more time enjoying the event. We are proud to support Memphis Athletics as it creates a more seamless experience for its passionate fan base.”
Genius brings together POS software, payments and operational tools in an enterprise-grade platform designed for stadiums, venues and other complex foodservice environments. By providing a clearer view of sales and operations, Genius can help organizations adjust to demand, improve throughput and make more informed decisions—supporting greater efficiency and revenue opportunities while delivering the faster, easier purchasing experience fans expect.
“Our partnership with Global Payments has allowed us to take another significant step forward in modernizing the fan experience at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium,” said Trent Wilks, general manager of Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. “Genius provides a faster, more convenient way for fans to order and pay, helping them spend less time waiting in concession lines and more time enjoying Memphis Tigers Football. Behind the scenes, the technology also gives us greater visibility and control over our food and beverage operations, allowing us to operate more efficiently during the high-demand environment of game day. Global Payments is more than a technology provider; they are a trusted partner who understands our goals and will help us continue elevating the stadium experience for years to come.”
The agreement expands the sports and venue technology footprint of Global Payments, which serves 160 stadiums and venues around the world, including every major sports league in the U.S., college football stadiums, football stadiums in Europe and more.

U.S. Bank Names Massuci and Quevedo to Payments Sales Leadership Team
summary:
U.S. Bank has named two new leaders to its Payments: Merchant and Institutional (PMI) Sales Distribution team. Lauren Massuci has joined as head of Financial Institutions Group (FIG) Sales, and Jose Quevedo is head of Diversified Industries Sales. Both report to Peter Geronimo, executive vice president and head of PMI Sales Distribution, Institutional Client Group (ICG).
Lauren Massuci
Massuci brings more than 18 years of treasury management sales, payments and business development experience to the role. Before joining U.S. Bank, she was senior vice president and Treasury Management Sales leader within PNC’s Financial Institutions Group. Prior to that, she was with Citi’s Treasury and Trade Solutions organization in sales and leadership roles supporting institutional clients. Most recently at Citi, she led the Client Executive team covering the technology, e-commerce and communications sectors.
“Financial institutions are operating in a rapidly evolving payments environment, and I’m excited to join U.S. Bank at such an important time for the industry,” said Massuci. “I look forward to working with our teams and clients to help financial institutions navigate change, identify opportunities and advance their payments strategies.”
Lauren earned her bachelor’s degree in business administration and entrepreneurship from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. She lives in the Chicago area with her husband, Nick, and their three children.
Jose Quevedo
Quevedo leads payment sales for Diversified industries, including global industrials and services, commercial real estate, aerospace and defense, energy, and utilities. The organization was designed to align PMI Sales Distribution more closely with U.S. Bank’s industry-focused approach within ICG.
Quevedo has more than 18 years of experience across treasury management, payments, merchant services, liquidity and working capital solutions. Most recently, Quevedo served as PMI Sales division manager for the Midwest region, leading sales strategy and execution across mid-cap and large corporate banking clients.
“Businesses are seeing the value of modern payment capabilities in delivering efficiency, intelligent decisions and loyalty among their clients through simple, easy payment experiences,” said Quevedo. “They’re looking for a partner who understands their industry, listens to their needs and works closely with them to develop solutions.”
Originally from Venezuela, Jose lives in Waconia, Minnesota, with his wife, Michelle, and their five children, ranging in age from 5 to 20. Outside of work, he enjoys coaching his son's soccer teams, traveling with his family, and embarking on road trips whenever possible.
U.S. Bank’s PMI Sales Distribution organization partners with ICG to connect larger business clients with the bank’s payment capabilities and provide holistic relationship management and client experiences.
“Clients turn to us for guidance on pressing payment challenges because we can deliver holistic solutions that help them achieve their goals and best serve their customers,” said Geronimo. “Lauren and Jose have a strong understanding of how clients are navigating change, and their experience will strengthen how we help businesses address increasingly complex payment needs.”
